text: An enum is a set of named constant values grouped under one type — perfect for fixed choices.
Instead of scattering magic numbers or loose strings, you define meaningful names like RED, GREEN, and BLUE.
Each member has both a name and a value, which you can access separately.
[chuckle] So Color dot RED reads clearly, and its value one is tucked away underneath.
[sniff] Enums compare by identity, so checking if a choice equals Color dot GREEN is both safe and readable.
No more accidentally comparing against a mistyped string that silently fails.
You can loop over an enum too, walking through every member in order.
[sigh] That makes enums great for menus, states, and any fixed set of options in your program.
[groan] Reach for an enum whenever a variable should only ever hold one of a small, known set of values.
